analysis.title: Magna International Inc. (MGA): 2026 EPS guidance unchanged; Ability to offset difficult market/industry dynamics with company specific efforts in focus; 3Q26 wrap
key_insights: Magna reported 3Q26 adjusted EBIT of $683 mn and adjusted EPS of $1.83, above the Street ($623 mn, $1.58) and GS ($611 mn, $1.51). Revenue was $10.1 bn, in line with the Street at $10.1 bn and GS at $10.2 bn.

Magna lowered its CY26 revenue guidance midpoint to $41.6 bn (down 1% yoy) from $41.9 bn, and narrowed the adjusted EBIT margin range to 6.3%-6.5% from 6.3%-6.6%, citing lower China vehicle production and program mix.
CY26 adjusted EPS guidance was narrowed to $6.85-$7.15 from $6.70-$7.30, with the $7.00 midpoint unchanged. Magna expects lower net interest expense and a lower tax rate.
CY26 FCF guidance was raised to $1.85 bn-$1.90 bn from $1.75 bn-$1.85 bn, and capex guidance is about $1.5 bn (from $1.5 bn-$1.6 bn).

Implied 4Q26 guidance at the midpoint is revenue $10.2 bn, adjusted EBIT $745 mn, margin 7.3% and adjusted EPS $1.93. This compares with GS prior at $10.6 bn/$867 mn/8.2%/$2.27 and the Street at $10.5 bn/$832 mn/7.9%/$2.23.

Operating margin rose about 90 bp yoy in 3Q, partly from the timing of recoveries. Operational excellence is tracking toward 50 bp of improvement in 2026 versus an initial 35-40 bp, with another 35-40 bp targeted for 2027.

Input costs were a 50 bp headwind in 3Q, and management expects a similar-size headwind in 4Q. Steel and aluminum are covered by resell or pass-through mechanisms, about 40% of resins is index-protected, and DRAM and electronic components show the largest cost increases, with recoveries to be negotiated with customers.

Magna repurchased $529 mn of shares and paid $129 mn of dividends in 3Q on adjusted FCF of about $584 mn. It completed its prior buyback in October and its board approved a new NCIB for 25.8 mn shares.

Magna grew 0.5% over its weighted markets in 3Q (1% excluding Complete Vehicles). For CY26 it now expects growth roughly in line with weighted vehicle production, versus 0-2% (1-3% ex Complete Vehicles) previously.

GS keeps its Sell rating, citing Magna's historically below-average growth over market in a sluggish production backdrop, EMEA exposure to tariffs and competition, and incremental input cost pressure shared with other tier 1 suppliers.
GS raised its 12-month price target to $56 from $55 (C$78 from C$77 for MG.TO), based on 7X applied to normalized EPS of $8.05 (from $7.90). This implies 12.3% downside from $63.82.
Magna is upfitting vehicles for Waymo in Arizona and is now working on two new vehicle models. Divestitures of low-margin businesses (Lighting, Rooftop Systems) are largely complete.
GS CY26/27/28 EPS estimates moved to $7.05/$7.65/$8.25 from $7.00/$7.60/$8.20 on lower share count, lower interest expense and lower revenue. Magna holds an investor day in November.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Sell on below-average growth over market, EMEA tariff and competition exposure and input cost pressure, despite a 3Q beat. Price target rose to $56 from $55, implying 12.3% downside.

sector_views.rationale: GS flags a sluggish production backdrop, incremental input cost pressure across tier 1 suppliers (DRAM, electronics, resins) and tariff exposure in EMEA.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported (10/30) non-GAAP EPS $1.83 vs Street consensus $1.58 and GS estimate $1.51.
3Q26 reported adjusted EBIT $683 mn (6.8% margin) vs Street $623 mn (6.2%) and GS $611 mn (6.0%). Revenue $10,059 mn vs Street $10,111 mn and GS $10,156 mn.
CY26 guidance: adjusted EPS $6.85-$7.15 (Street est $7.05, GS prior $7.00), revenue $41.2 bn-$42.0 bn (Street est $41.9 bn), adjusted EBIT margin 6.3%-6.5%, FCF $1.85 bn-$1.90 bn.
Implied 4Q26 adjusted EPS at the guidance midpoint is $1.93, versus Street estimate $2.23 and GS prior estimate $2.27, a $0.30 and $0.34 shortfall.
GS estimates CY26/27/28 EPS at $7.05/$7.65/$8.25 (prior $7.00/$7.60/$8.20); CY26 EBITDA $4,240.6 mn and revenue $41,653 mn.

risk_factors: Incremental input cost pressure, especially DRAM and electronic components, where recoveries must be negotiated with customers.
Tariffs and competition in EMEA could make growth more difficult.
Lower China vehicle production and unfavorable program mix.
Historically below-average growth over market in a sluggish production backdrop.
Upside risks to the Sell: share gains, higher content per vehicle, faster margin and FCF improvement, a better auto cycle or more favorable tariff rules.
